slides.narration: Chapter 29: The Last Free Number. The electroweak scale — the energy at which particles acquire mass — is predicted by a self-referential equation whose solution matches the measurement to 0.66 parts per million.

The Higgs vacuum expectation value v comes out to 246.2195 GeV. The measured value is 246.21965. That is a match to 0.66 parts per million — six hundred times more precise than the framework's own theoretical uncertainty. Zero adjustable parameters.

The equation is self-referential: the mass determines the screening depth, which determines the coupling, which determines the mass. The fixed point of this loop — the one value where the cycle is self-consistent — is the physical mass. The loop closes at exactly one number.
